questions.stem: Glucocorticoids act on which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Glucocorticoids act on the intracellular cytoplasmic receptors. 

They diffuse into cytosol and bind to the cytoplasmic receptors and influence nuclear changes by activation of the receptor. 





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no: 850

questions.stem: Glucocorticoids do not have permissive action on which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Glucocorticoids do not have permissive action on bradykinin. They inhibit inflammatory mediators such as histamine, bradykinin, and eicosanoids. 

Glucocorticoids possess permissive action on the vasoconstrictor effect of angiotensin and lipolytic action of adrenaline and noradrenaline. In the absence of glucocorticoids, these hormones have low activity but the presence enhances their activity several folds.





Tripathi's Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology 7th Edition, Page no: 284, 285

questions.stem: A pregnant woman diagnosed with Cushing's syndrome does not want surgery and requests medical treatment. Which of the following drugs can be recommended?
questions.solutionHtml:
Metyrapone can be recommended as it is approved in the treatment of pregnant women with Cushing's syndrome. It inhibits the synthesis of cortisol by inhibiting steroid 11 β-hydroxylase reversibly. 

Cushing’s syndrome (CS) is a manifestation of symptoms that are precipitated by excessive cortisol production. Transsphenoidal surgery, radiation, and pharmacotherapy constitute the standard treatment for tumor-related causes of CS (e.g. pituitary adenoma).

The three main pharmacological approaches are:

  • Cortisol synthesis inhibitors: Ketoconazole, metyrapone, mitotane, etomidate, aminoglutethimide
  • ACTH secretion inhibitors: Cyproheptadine, pasireotide, octreotide, cabergoline
  • Glucocorticoid receptor antagonist: Mifepristone

Note: Metyrapone is also used to test the hypothalamic-pituitary feedback pathway in the diagnosis of Cushing syndrome.





Katzung's Basic and Clinical Pharmacology 12/E (Lange Basic Science), Page no. 710
Online Resource, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19939210/

questions.stemHtml: The enzyme A in the following image corresponds to?
questions.solutionHtml:
"A" here corresponds to 11-beta-HSD2 (11β-Hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase2). It converts active cortisol to inactive cortisone. 

Cortisol is active and can bind to both glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoid receptors whereas cortisone is inactive and does not bind to either. The selective inactivation of cortisol is required in certain sites such as the distal nephron so that the specific autoregulatory responses to aldosterone can be achieved.

Therefore, cortisol (active) is metabolized to cortisone (inactive) by 11-beta-HSD2 in the kidney, so as to protect renal mineralocorticoid receptors from cortisol binding. Some tissues, like the liver, can convert inactive cortisone back to active cortisol through an enzyme called 11-beta-HSD1 ("B" in the image). This completes the “cortisone–cortisol shuttle” because the kidney can inactivate cortisol where it is not needed and the liver can reactivate it afterward.




However, when circulating cortisol levels are very high, as in severe Cushing syndrome, they can overwhelm this protective mechanism, allowing cortisol to bind to and activate the mineralocorticoid receptor. This leads to volume expansion, hypertension, and hypokalemia often observed in hypercortisolism. A mutation of 11-beta-HSD2 also causes a similar clinical picture and is the reason for the syndrome of apparent mineralocorticoid excess.

17β-Hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase and 3β-Hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase are involved in the metabolism of sex steroids.






Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 14th Edition, Page no: 1009
Online Resource, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12809455/
Online Resource, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3357308/

questions.stem: Which of the following is a prodrug?
questions.solutionHtml:
Prednisone is a prodrug.

It is a synthetic glucocorticoid that is biologically inert until converted via hepatic metabolism (11-beta HSD1) to the active component, prednisolone.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no. 853

questions.stem: A patient with moderate COVID-19 was started on a long-acting glucocorticoid. Which of the following drugs could it be?
questions.solutionHtml:
Dexamethasone is the longest acting glucocorticoid. Its t1/2 is >36 hours.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no: 853

questions.stem: Highest mineralocorticoid activity is seen with which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
The highest mineralocorticoid activity is seen with aldosterone.

However, it cannot be used clinically. The highest mineralocorticoid activity in a drug that is used clinically is fludrocortisone.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist?
questions.solutionHtml:
Metyrapone is not a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist.

It is a selective inhibitor of 11β-hydroxylase and thereby reduces cortisol and corticosterone synthesis.

Options A and B - Spironolactone and eplerenone are aldosterone antagonist that is used in hypertension and chronic CHF for reversing the effects of aldosterone

Option C - Drospirenone is a 4th generation progestin used as an oral contraceptive having mineralocorticoid antagonist action





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page No 858
Katzung Basic and Clinical Pharmacology - 14th Edition, Page No 716

questions.stem: A woman diagnosed with Sheehan's syndrome is planned for the initiation of hormone replacement. Glucocorticoids should be administered prior to thyroxine supplementation due to what concern?

options.label: C
options.text: Decrease in the metabolism of glucocorticoids

questions.solutionHtml:
Glucocorticoids are administered before initiating treatment with thyroid hormones as administration of thyroxine can precipitate acute adrenal insufficiency.

In the case of combined adrenal insufficiency and hypothyroidism, as in panhypopituitarism (due to surgery or Sheehan's syndrome), adrenal insufficiency is generally treated first. This is because giving thyroxine first can enhance cortisol clearance and precipitate an adrenal crisis. Also, levothyroxine increases the basal metabolic rate (BMR) leading to an increased requirement of cortisol, which if not met can also precipitate an adrenal crisis. 





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no. 856

questions.stem: A pregnant woman came for routine antenatal screening. During prenatal testing, the fetus was suspected to have congenital adrenal hyperplasia. What is the drug of choice for treating the fetus in-utero?
questions.solutionHtml:
The drug of choice for treating the fetus in-utero when suspected of having congenital adrenal hyperplasia is dexamethasone.

Dexamethasone readily crosses the placenta and suppresses the secretion of steroids and androgens by fetal adrenal glands. If started by 6 weeks of gestation, it reduces the virilization of external genitalia in affected females.

Chorionic villus biopsy is then performed to determine the sex and the genotype of the fetus and therapy is only continued if the fetus is an affected female.

This is not widely accepted currently due to insufficient data on long-term risks especially in unaffected females and males who derive no benefit from the treatment.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no 856
Nelson textbook of pediatrics 21st edition, Page no. 2976

questions.stem: A patient is started on hormone replacement for chronic adrenal insufficiency. What is the replacement dose of hydrocortisone that has to be given (in mg/day)?
questions.solutionHtml:
The replacement dose of hydrocortisone for chronic adrenal insufficiency is 20 mg/day.

The treatment of chronic adrenal insufficiency (not in crisis) requires glucocorticoid replacement at a dose that replaces the physiologic daily cortisol production. This is achieved by administering an oral replacement dose of 15-25mg Hydrocortisone. 
A midpoint dose of 20mg is given in 2-3 divided doses: 10mg + 5mg + 5mg. 
A higher morning dose is given at 8:30 am (usually 1/2 to 2/3 of the total dose). The next dose is given at 1:30 pm and in the evening (4:30-5:00 pm). This is to follow the normal circadian rhythm. 





Online Resource, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9276933/
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 21st Edition, Page no: 2972

questions.stem: A pregnant woman at 33 weeks of gestation presents to your antenatal clinic with preterm labour. Which corticosteroid will you administer for stimulation of fetal lung maturation?
questions.solutionHtml:
Betamethasone is indicated for the stimulation of fetal lung maturation in preterm labor.

As compared to cortisol, betamethasone binds to maternal proteins less and has less placental metabolism. This allows increased transfer to the fetus. Additionally, infants exposed to betamethasone are less likely to require postnatal resuscitation. 2 doses of 12 mg each are administered 18-24 hours apart when the delivery is anticipated before 34 weeks of gestation.

Dexamethasone is another long-acting glucocorticoid that can be given. It has benefits such as less risk of intraventricular hemorrhage and a shorter length of stay in the NICU.





Katzung's Basic and Clinical Pharmacology 12/E (Lange Basic Science), Page no: 705
Online Resource, https://www.acog.org/-/media/Committee-Opinions/Committee-on-Obstetric-Practice/co713.pdf?dmc=1&ts=20171021T1027416805
Journal, Cochrane; https://www.cochrane.org/CD006764/PREG_corticosteroid-treatments-before-early-birth-for-reducing-death-lung-problems-and-brain-haemorrhage-in-babies

questions.stem: A patient with chronic adrenal insufficiency is on long term corticosteroid therapy. Which of the following side effects is he unlikely to experience?
questions.solutionHtml:
Corticosteroid therapy does not cause muscular hypertrophy and the patient is unlikely to experience it as a side effect.

Excess glucocorticoid activity results in muscle wasting and myopathy while excess mineralocorticoid activity results in hypokalemia and causes muscle weakness.

Options B and C: Peptic ulceration and psychosis are known adverse effects of corticosteroids.

Option D: Glucocorticoids with some mineralocorticoid activity will result in sodium and water retention and may cause hypertension.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no: 851

questions.stem: You are planning to add oral steroids to manage a case of severe asthma. Presence of which of the following comorbidities is not a relative contraindication for starting the medication?
questions.solutionHtml:
Eczematous skin diseases are not a contraindication for the use of oral corticosteroids. In fact, they are highly effective and are indicated in this condition.

All the contraindications to steroids are relative because of the life-saving nature of steroids.

Risk-benefit should be assessed cautiously when initiating steroids in the following conditions:

  • Diabetes mellitus
  • Hypertension
  • Peptic ulcer
  • Viral and fungal infections
  • Tuberculosis and other infections
  • Osteoporosis
  • Herpes simplex keratitis
  • Epilepsy
  • CHF
  • Renal failure




Tripathi's Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology 7th Edition, Page no: 294
Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no: 857

questions.stem: A 54-year-old woman is being evaluated for chronic back pain. She mentions that she had been on corticosteroids for asthma since childhood. Which of the following actions of the drug would not cause her condition?
questions.solutionHtml:
Chronic back pain following long term corticosteroid therapy is suggestive of osteoporosis. Glucocorticoids do not inhibit of the action of osteoclasts.

It causes stimulation of osteoclasts and increases bone resorption.

Mechanism of glucocorticoids induced osteoporosis:

  • Inhibition of gonadal steroidal hormones
  • Reduced gastrointestinal absorption of calcium
  • Secondary effect of decreased calcium absorption: increased parathyroid hormone leading to further resorption
  • Suppressive action on osteoblasts
  • Stimulation of osteoclasts




Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9e, pg 1125

questions.stem: Osteonecrosis following glucocorticoid therapy is most commonly associated with which site?
questions.solutionHtml:
The femoral head is the most frequently affected site by osteonecrosis due to glucocorticoid therapy.

The earliest symptoms are joint pain and stiffness. When patients on steroid therapy develop hip, shoulder or knee pain, osteonecrosis must be considered and ruled out.

Options B and D - It can also affect the distal femur and humeral head 

Option C - Osteonecrosis of the jaw is associated with the use of bisphosphonates 





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page No. 855

questions.stem: A patient with Cushing’s syndrome has very high levels of ACTH. Which of the following is a CRH preparation that can be used to determine if it is a pituitary source or an ectopic source?
questions.solutionHtml:
Corticorelin is a corticotrophin-releasing hormone (CRH) preparation used in CRH stimulation test which helps to differentiate between a pituitary source and an ectopic source for ACTH-dependent hypercortisolism. 

Pituitary tumors tend to be sensitive to CRH stimulation and responds with a rise in cortisol while ectopic tumors do not usually respond. Ectopic sources of ACTH include carcinoid, medullary thyroid carcinoma, and pheochromocytoma.

It can also be used to test the HPA axis.

Option A - Gonadorelin is a recombinant GnRH.

Option C - Ganirelix is a GnRH antagonist.

Option D - Cosyntropin is a synthetic preparation of ACTH.

 





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no. 848
Online Resource, https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/Corticorelin-ovine-triflutate

questions.stem: Which of the following is a steroid receptor antagonist that can be given to a patient with Cushing’s syndrome due to ectopic ACTH?
questions.solutionHtml:
Mifepristone is a steroid receptor antagonist that can be used in Cushing’s syndrome.

It is used in Cushing’s syndrome especially in inoperable cases with ectopic ACTH secretion or adrenal carcinoma.

Options A, B, and D - Ketoconazole, metyrapone, and aminoglutethimide reduce steroid synthesis by enzyme inhibition.





Katzung Basic and Clinical Pharmacology - 14th Edition, Page no: 717

questions.stem: Which of the following intravenous anaesthetics can be used for acute control of hypercortisolism?
questions.solutionHtml:
The intravenous anesthetic that can be used for acute control of hypercortisolism is etomidate.

Etomidate at sub-hypnotic doses inhibits cortisol secretion by selectively inhibiting 11-beta-hydroxylase activity. 

It is used off-label to treat hypercortisolism when rapid control is needed and the patient is not able to take oral medication.





Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition, Page no: 859

questions.stem: A patient is diagnosed with inoperable adrenocortical carcinoma and needs medical adrenalectomy. Which of the following drugs could be used for him?
questions.solutionHtml:
Mitotane is used for medical adrenalectomy in this patient.

It has a non-selective toxic action on the adrenal cortex. It causes suppression of adrenal cortex hormone secretion comparable to that of adrenalectomy. 





Katzung's Basic and Clinical Pharmacology 12/E (Lange Basic Science), Page no: 711

questions.stem: Which of the following antifungal drugs can be used in the treatment of a patient with Cushing syndrome?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ketoconazole can be used in the treatment of Cushing syndrome for symptomatic control.

It is a non-selective inhibitor of adrenal and gonadal steroid synthesis. These actions are more apparent at higher doses than those used for fungal infections.





Katzung Basic and Clinical Pharmacology 14th Edition, Page no 715
